claim: Supermicro's 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026: 'One supplier accounted for a significant portion of our total purchases in fiscal year 2026 of 63.1%' (not named); purchases from the related parties Ablecom and Compuware were 2.1% of cost of sales in fiscal year 2026 (Ablecom coordinates chassis manufacturing; Compuware makes subassemblies, particularly power supplies); one customer accounted for 10% or more of net sales in fiscal year 2026; systems are mostly made in San Jose, with assembly and test also in Taiwan, the Netherlands and Malaysia. Dell's 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 30, 2026 says it owns manufacturing facilities in the United States, Malaysia, China, Brazil, India, Poland and Ireland, that 'significant portions of our products are assembled by contract manufacturers, primarily in locations in Asia', and that its AI solutions have been bought primarily by a small number of larger customers and cloud service providers. Neither filing names a GPU, CPU or memory supplier or a customer in the text read.

record_sources.title: Micron Technology, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 3, 2026

claim: Micron's 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 3, 2026 states that 'approximately one-half of our total revenue was from our top ten customers' in each of the last three years, with no customer named; that it manufactures in its own facilities in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China and India; that a majority of its 2026 DRAM output came from its Taiwan fabs; and that it has funding agreements for the construction of fab facilities in Idaho and New York and to expand and modernize its fab in Virginia. HBM is supplied to unnamed data center customers.
